nodes.label: NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform
nodes.what: A rack-scale AI platform that combines Rubin GPUs, Vera CPUs, networking, storage and software as one system.
nodes.why_matters: Anchor. Rubin changes the unit of deployment from a discrete accelerator toward a tightly integrated rack and pod.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls HBM4, co-designed chips, high-speed networking, liquid cooling, power delivery and qualified rack manufacturing.

nodes.label: NVIDIA Rubin GPU
nodes.what: The GPU component of Vera Rubin, with HBM4 memory, NVLink 6 and a new Transformer Engine.
nodes.why_matters: It is the main compute and memory-bandwidth element in the platform.
nodes.if_scales: Raises demand for HBM4 stacks, advanced GPU packaging and NVLink-connected rack integration.

nodes.label: NVIDIA Vera CPU
nodes.what: The CPU component designed for agentic workloads, orchestration and CPU-based environments alongside Rubin GPUs.
nodes.why_matters: Rubin’s rack is co-designed around CPU-GPU communication rather than GPU-only compute.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls CPU production, NVLink-C2C integration, memory modules and liquid-cooled CPU racks.

nodes.label: HBM4 memory
nodes.what: High-bandwidth memory used by Rubin; NVIDIA describes up to 288 GB and 22 TB/s per GPU.
nodes.why_matters: Memory bandwidth and capacity feed the GPU’s compute units and long-context workloads.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls qualified HBM4 stacks, logic base dies, stacking, test and memory-supplier capacity.

nodes.label: HBM4 12-Hi stacks
nodes.what: Twelve-high HBM4 stacks specified in NVIDIA’s Rubin GPU architecture description.
nodes.why_matters: Stack height and yield affect usable memory per package and the number of qualified stacks per GPU.
nodes.if_scales: Increases exposure to stack assembly, bonding and known-good-stack testing.

nodes.label: NVLink 6 switch
nodes.what: Sixth-generation switch fabric connecting Rubin GPUs at rack scale, with 3.6 TB/s per-GPU scale-up bandwidth in NVIDIA materials.
nodes.why_matters: It lets many GPUs communicate as one tightly coupled domain.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls switch silicon, optical/electrical links, rack integration and validation.

nodes.label: ConnectX-9 SuperNIC
nodes.what: NVIDIA networking component for scale-out communication between Rubin systems and the wider AI factory.
nodes.why_matters: The rack still depends on traffic leaving the local NVLink domain.
nodes.if_scales: Raises demand for high-speed network adapters, cables/transceivers and fabric qualification.

nodes.label: BlueField-4 DPU
nodes.what: Data-processing unit used in Rubin’s storage and infrastructure paths to offload data services and control functions.
nodes.why_matters: Rubin’s platform includes storage and infrastructure processing, not only GPU compute.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls DPU silicon, storage integration and software validation across the rack and pod.

nodes.label: Spectrum-6 Ethernet
nodes.what: NVIDIA Ethernet switch platform for rack-to-rack scale-out networking in Rubin AI factories.
nodes.why_matters: A Rubin pod requires a network fabric beyond the local NVLink domain.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls switch silicon, network optics and deployment qualification.

nodes.label: Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics
nodes.what: Co-packaged optical switch path NVIDIA describes for power-efficient, high-scale Ethernet networking.
nodes.why_matters: Photonics can move more traffic across the factory without relying only on electrical front-panel links.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls optical engines, lasers, packaging, fiber plant and photonics test.

nodes.label: Vera Rubin NVL72 rack
nodes.what: A rack integrating 72 Rubin GPUs, 36 Vera CPUs, NVLink 6, ConnectX-9 and BlueField-4 according to NVIDIA’s platform materials.
nodes.why_matters: It is the clearest documented unit where Rubin’s component dependencies become a deployable system.
nodes.if_scales: Raises rack manufacturing, liquid cooling, power delivery and site commissioning requirements.

nodes.label: Advanced GPU packaging
nodes.what: Multi-die semiconductor packaging that joins compute dies and HBM into a usable GPU package.
nodes.why_matters: Rubin GPU output requires package integration; public sources establish the process need but not a Rubin-specific packaging supplier here.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls package substrates, interposers, bonding, inspection and package test.

nodes.label: Leading-edge logic fabrication
nodes.what: Wafer fabrication for Rubin and Vera silicon using a leading-edge process.
nodes.why_matters: The platform depends on complex logic dies before packaging and rack integration.
nodes.if_scales: Raises demand for qualified wafer starts and process yield; the Rubin supplier is not named in this map.

nodes.label: Qualified HBM4 suppliers
nodes.what: Memory companies publicly connected to HBM4 production or Rubin memory development.
nodes.why_matters: Rubin needs qualified memory, but a public supplier mention does not prove sole-source status or a current shortage.
nodes.if_scales: Qualification and ramp decisions could concentrate exposure among the suppliers that clear Rubin requirements.

nodes.label: Rubin manufacturing partners
nodes.what: NVIDIA’s broad group of server makers and supply-chain partners manufacturing or shipping Rubin-based systems.
nodes.why_matters: The platform is delivered through a partner ecosystem rather than by NVIDIA alone.
nodes.if_scales: Rack production, testing and logistics become part of the platform’s effective capacity.

nodes.label: Direct liquid cooling
nodes.what: Liquid-cooling infrastructure used by Rubin racks and systems to remove heat at high compute density.
nodes.why_matters: Rubin system deployment depends on a facility able to accept and operate liquid-cooled hardware.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls cold plates, coolant distribution, heat rejection, service capability and site retrofits.

nodes.label: AI-factory power delivery
nodes.what: Grid connection, distribution and power equipment serving high-density AI racks.
nodes.why_matters: A completed rack cannot operate without enough electrical capacity and suitable distribution.
nodes.if_scales: Can shift exposure from silicon supply to transformers, grid connections, generation and commissioning.

nodes.label: AI factory deployment
nodes.what: The facility, network, storage, cooling and operations layer that turns Rubin racks into usable AI capacity.
nodes.why_matters: Rubin is designed as a rack/pod system; deployment depends on the whole facility, not only the GPU.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls construction, networking, storage, power, cooling and operations at the same time.

nodes.label: NVIDIA Blackwell platform
nodes.what: The prior NVIDIA platform used as the comparison baseline for Rubin’s documented changes.
nodes.why_matters: The comparison helps separate new Rubin dependencies from dependencies already present in Blackwell.
nodes.if_scales: Some Rubin changes are relative improvements or additions, not entirely new supply-chain categories.

nodes.label: HBM3E memory
nodes.what: High-bandwidth memory used in Blackwell-era accelerator systems.
nodes.why_matters: NVIDIA describes Rubin’s HBM4 as a change from the HBM3E generation used in Blackwell materials.
nodes.if_scales: HBM3E and HBM4 qualification may overlap during the platform transition.

nodes.label: NVLink 5 switch
nodes.what: Fifth-generation NVLink and switch technology associated with Blackwell systems.
nodes.why_matters: NVIDIA describes NVLink 6 as the next generation with higher scale-up bandwidth.
nodes.if_scales: The transition changes switch silicon and validation requirements, but does not prove a shortage.

nodes.label: Micron Technology
nodes.what: HBM4 memory supplier that says its 36GB 12-Hi product is designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin.
nodes.why_matters: This is a named Rubin memory relationship with a company-reported volume-shipment claim.
nodes.if_scales: Rubin ramp visibility would depend partly on qualification and delivery of Micron’s HBM4 configuration.

nodes.label: SK hynix
nodes.what: Memory supplier that announced a multi-year NVIDIA partnership including memory development for Vera Rubin.
nodes.why_matters: The announcement establishes development work, not a disclosed Rubin shipment or sole-source position.
nodes.if_scales: Further qualification or shipment disclosures would make its Rubin role more precise.

nodes.label: TSMC
nodes.what: Wafer and chip manufacturing partner named by NVIDIA in its Rubin supply-chain description.
nodes.why_matters: Rubin depends on leading-edge logic fabrication, but public sources here do not identify the exact Rubin process or output allocation.
nodes.if_scales: A Rubin ramp could increase exposure to qualified wafer capacity and advanced packaging availability.

nodes.label: Foxconn
nodes.what: Electronics and server manufacturer that has exhibited full-system Vera Rubin NVL72 racks and described rack, cooling, power and integration capabilities.
nodes.why_matters: Foxconn is a concrete system-builder example, but an exhibition or build announcement does not establish shipment volume.
nodes.if_scales: More Rubin deployments could increase demand for Foxconn’s rack integration and manufacturing capacity.

nodes.label: Lenovo
nodes.what: System company whose NVIDIA announcement describes its Neptune liquid-cooling solution and manufacturing and service reach for the Rubin platform.
nodes.why_matters: The source supports a Rubin system and cooling relationship, not a disclosed production allocation or shipment volume.
nodes.if_scales: A Rubin ramp could increase the importance of qualified liquid-cooled system assembly and service coverage.

nodes.label: Vertiv
nodes.what: Power and cooling infrastructure company contributing simulation-ready designs to the NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI-factory reference design.
nodes.why_matters: This is an infrastructure-design relationship rather than proof that Vertiv supplies every Rubin site or rack.
nodes.if_scales: A ramp could expand demand for validated power, cooling, controls and deployment services around Rubin facilities.
